gemini.content:
### Movement I: Hyperbolic Sprawl

Had the High Imperial Ministry of Topography and Memory (*K.K. Ministerium für Topographie und Gedächtnis*) not decreed, in the damp autumn following the catastrophe of 1878, that the forgotten was merely a higher-order tensor of the unmeasured, I should never have descended into the subterranean galleries of the *Kataster des Unaussprechlichen* with a brass-geared theodolite strapped to my thoracic harness and a copper canister of vitriol-stabilized kerosene clutched in my calloused palm. It was the prevailing dogma of our master, Ignaz Harkanyi—who had sat equally at the feet of Camillo Sitte in the Technische Hochschule and Bernhard Riemann in the rain-choked lecture halls of Göttingen—that a city’s public space was not an inert tabula rasa of Haussmannian cuts and orthogonal paving, but rather an elastic, affective manifold wherein the collective psychic mass of municipal guilt exerted an absolute gravitational pull upon the load-bearing properties of limestone. 

```
================================================================================
OFFICIAL SURVEY LOGBOOK: SECTOR ℵ₁ (THIRD SUB-LEVEL)
K.K. Kataster des Unaussprechlichen – Bureau of Archival Metrology
Surveyor: Franziska von Thalheim (Chief Philologist-Surveyor, Class I)
Instrument: Troughton & Simms Non-Euclidean Theodolite No. IV (Merz Optik)
Reference Datum: S-1878-Brigittenau-Flut / Strike Archive (Vault 44-B)
================================================================================
INSTRUMENTAL MEASUREMENTS (RECORDED):
- Parallax Angle (Keystone α to Porphyry Pier β): 104° 17' 42"
- Gaussian Curvature (K): -0.0418 m⁻² (Hyperbolic/Pseudospherical)
- Metric Tensor Component (g_θθ): 1.184 ± 0.003
- Acoustic Resonant Pitch: 41.2 Hz (Sub-diapason; damp slate resonance)

SURVEYOR’S MARGINAL ANNOTATIONS (REDACTED FROM MINISTRY DISPATCH):
The vault has narrowed by three palms since the feast of St. Jude. The Ministry clerks in the Herrengasse have successfully struck the names of forty-two drowned textile dyers from the municipal pension ledger; consequently, the squinches over the eastern arcade have developed a severe, weeping torsional twist. The mortar smells of river silt and wet flannel. When I sight through the Merz reticle, the crosshairs do not bisect the datum mark on the plinth; they curve toward the shadow of Therese’s collarbone—which I have surreptitiously chiseled into the spandrel beneath the cornice, substituting the shear-strain coefficient for the precise curvature of her left clavicle as she lay upon the mud of the Brigittenau sluice.
================================================================================
```

Twelve years of continuous archival residency beneath the Ringstraße had taught me that a forgotten strike does not vanish into the ether of pure negation, but instead sinks through the permeable loess of the Danube basin until it lodges in Sector $\aleph_1$, warping the geometry of our sub-level until every archway becomes an asymptotic funnel. As I stepped past the perimeter gate of the Third Sub-level, the flickering aureole of the gas lanterns revealed a vestibule whose walls diverged at angles monstrously incompatible with the Euclidean plane: the pennants of the high ribbed vaults, instead of meeting at a tranquil, centralized keystone, stretched outward into an infinite hyperbolic horn, their ashlar joints oozing a pale, calcified slurry that tasted faintly of zinc and dried river-weed.

Here, the official history of the Danube inundation of February 1878—an event which the Emperor’s censors had successfully reduced in the public broadsheets to a "seasonal irregularity of the meltwaters," omitting entirely the six hundred drowned laborers of the Brigittenau canal-works who had barricaded themselves within the sluice-tunnels to demand twelve-hour wages—was preserved not as an immutable volume of calfskin codices, but as a vast, living stereotomy. Whenever a surviving widow in the Leopoldstadt died without passing the memory of that frozen morning to her grandchildren, the spatial metric of Sector $\aleph_1$ shuddered: a pier would shear along its cleavage plane, a flight of travertine stairs would contract by three-eighths of a millimeter per step, and the syntax of the original eyewitness depositions, inked upon heavy Austrian ragsheet, would spontaneously adjust its grammatic case structures, drifting from the robust certainty of the indicative past into the ghostly, conditional evasions of the *Konjunktiv*.

"Observe the squinch, Thalheim," Harkanyi had whispered to me a decade earlier, his lungs already whistling with the silicosis that would eventually turn his bronchial passages into a petrified fossil of the very catacombs he had surveyed. "The arch does not merely hold the ceiling; it holds the memory of what the city dared not bury under open sky. If Vienna forgets the sound of the ice-shatter against the timber caissons, the stone must bear the load of that silence. The stress-strain tensor is our true civic conscience."

I adjusted the vernier screw of my theodolite. The corridor before me did not extend in a straight line, nor did it describe a rational arc; rather, it uncoiled like a Riemann surface along a series of branch cuts, where each step forward required a calculation of Christoffel symbols merely to ensure that my right boot would land upon the same metric plane as my left. The air was thick, heavy with the suffocating sweetness of carbon monoxide leaking from the corroded iron pipe-lines that supplied the deep-gallery Welsbach mantles—a dull, narcotic fug that set my temples to thrumming with a rhythmic, sickening ache that mimic’d the very groaning of the granite. Or was it the stone itself that was drugged?

Before me lay the transverse gallery leading to Vault 44-B, within which resided the single remaining unredacted copy of the deposition of Josef Malek, the union foreman who had watched the imperial engineers deliberately open the weir gates to drown the strike-barracks under six feet of ice-sludge. If I did not reach the repository before the city’s centennial celebrations above completed the semantic absorption of the disaster, the chamber’s volume would reach absolute zero, crushing the text into an impenetrable grain of high-density slate and sealing the murder of my sister, Therese—who had carried the strike committee’s dispatches across the freezing canal—into the silent, structural mechanics of the imperial foundation.

I moved forward, my woolen surveyor’s skirts dragging through the thin film of subterranean runoff that trickled across the floor-slabs along non-Euclidean geodesics, the water pooling not in the hollows of the floor, but clinging in shimmering, inverted ribbons to the high, concave flanks of the Voronoi tessellations above my head.

---

   * **Prose Register:** Emulate the melancholic, measured cadence of W.G. Sebald (*Austerlitz*), the recursive architectural metaphysics of Jorge Luis Borges, and the claustrophobic rhythmic intensity of Thomas Bernhard.
   * **Syntactic Mechanics:** Utilize hypotactic sentence structures with subordinate clauses that mirror the nesting of vaulted chambers and corridors. Maintain an austere, clinical elegance that contrasts sharply with the encroaching psychological terror.
   * **Proscription:** Avoid all generic speculative cliches (e.g., no overt cosmic tentacles, no generic "haunted house" jump-scares, no magic portals, no pulpy sci-fi devices). The supernatural elements must remain strictly philological, mathematical, and spatial.

# THE PALEOGRAPHIC CATASTER OF MONTE NEBULOSO

## Being the Complete Survey Record of the Sanatorio del Silenzio, Compiled Under Commission of the Austro-Venetian Hydrographic Commission, Exclave of Kotor-Grado, 1973

---

## FRAGMENT I: THE SURVEYOR'S FIELD LOG

**Peristyle of Aorist Inflections — Eastern Transept, Axis 7****14 September 1973. Barometric pressure:741 mm. Light: hypaethral, unmediated.**

I enter the peristyle at06:42, bearing the theodolite, the graphite stylus, and the lexicon of the *Vetus Illyrica* in its third, water-damaged edition, which Margot annotated in the margins during the survey of '69, before the collapse, before the—

I set this aside. I enter.

The Peristyle of Aorist Inflections extends before me in a single, unbroken processional axis of some forty-three metres, though I must record immediately that this measurement is provisional, contingent upon the tense in which I choose to inscribe it, for the architect—Kovačević, that apostate of Wagner's atelier, that renegade who took Loos's *Ornament und Verbrechen* and inverted it into a grammar of structural forgetting—designed the cyclopean stereotomy of these walls such that the poché, the very thickness of the load-bearing limestone, is conjugated. I do not mean this metaphorically. The ashlar blocks are cut to tolerances of 0.3 millimetres and set in courses that correspond to the seven aspectual stems of the *Vetus Illyrica* verb, so that the wall's depth—its resistance to the eye, its opacity, its refusal to be seen through—is a function of temporal reference. I measure the corridor in the active voice, *I traverse the peristyle*, and the poché reads at1.2 metres, the stereotomic joints clean and rational, the post-tensioned ferroconcrete lintels above holding their 1911 tension with a sound like a held breath, and the hypaethral light falls from the open oculus in a single column that strikes the floor in a parallelogram of white.

I note this. I record: *I traverse. I observe. I measure.*

The corridor holds at forty-three metres. The walls hold at 1.2 metres. The light is clean and architectural and indifferent.

And then, because the lexicon demands it, because the grammatical protocol of the Cataster requires that every spatial observation be rendered in the full paradigm of the *Vetus Illyrica* before it may be entered into the register, I am compelled to write the passive: *The peristyle is traversed. The measurement is taken. The light is received by the stone.*The walls thicken.

Not quickly. Not with violence. But with the slow, tectonic patience of a sentence being diagrammed by an impatient hand. The poché swells to 1.4,1.6 metres. The stereotomic joints narrow as though the ashlar courses are drawing breath, compressing, and the ferroconcrete lintels groan at a frequency I feel in the molars rather than hear, a subsonic complaint of calcium silicate under revised load. The parallelogram of hypaethral light contracts by perhaps fifteen centimetres on its western edge, as though the oculus above has blinked. I step backward. The corridor, which was forty-three metres, is now—I pace it, I pace it twice, I count my heel-to-toe lengths with the obsessive regularity Margot taught me in the surveying courses at the Polytechnikum, and it is now thirty-nine metres, and the walls, which I can press both palms against if I extend my arms fully, are closer than they were, and the grammar of the space has shifted from an assertion to a reception, from a subject acting upon the world to a world acting upon a subject, and I understand, with the cold clarity of a man reading his own autopsy report, that the corridor is not shrinking. The corridor is being *remembered at a slower rate*, and the *Vetus Illyrica* noun for *corridor*—*stĕna-vekt*—does not denote a passage between walls but rather the half-life of one's recollection of having once walked a passage between walls, and in the passive voice, in the voice of the patient rather than the agent, that half-life shortens, and the stone, obedient to its conjugation, closes.

I write, quickly, in the active: *I walk. I see. I am here.*

The walls hesitate. The poché holds at 1.5 metres. The light steadies.But I have lost four metres of corridor, and I do not know how to decline them back.

I press forward, because the commission demands forward, because the Hydrographic Commission in its damp offices above the harbour expects the Cataster completed by Michaelmas, because I cannot return to the city where Margot's phonetics laboratory sits locked and chalk-dusted, her spectrographs still pinned to the corkboard like the wings of moths she intended to name but never did. I press forward into the deeper chambers, where the aorist gives way to the imperfect, where the verb stems thicken and the ceilings lower and the light—

The light is no longer hypaethral. There is no oculus here. There is only the grey luminescence of the limestone itself, as though the stone remembers having once been illuminated and has not yet finished forgetting.

I record the dimensions. I record them in the active voice. I do not stop speaking. I do not stop saying *I* and *I* and *I*, because I have observed, in the three hours since I crossed the threshold, that the third person singular—the *he walks, the surveyor measures*—causes the rooms to multiply. I turned a corner into what should have been the Apodyterium of the Southern Wing and found instead three Apodyteria, identical, recursive, each containing a smaller Apodyterium within it, like a sentence embedded within its own subordinate clause, and I walked through all three before the grammar released me, and in the innermost room I found, scratched into the plaster in Margot's left-handed script, a single word in the *Vetus Illyrica* that I cannot yet parse, a word in a case the lexicon does not list, and I did not copy it, I did not copy it, I walked out and I did not copy it, and the corridor behind me sealed with a sound like a book closing in an empty library.The barometric pressure is falling. The light is failing. I will continue into the Nave of the Perfective tomorrow, if the grammar permits a tomorrow, if I can conjugate the morning in a voice that does not collapse the ceiling.

I am here. I walk. I measure.

I am here.

---

## FRAGMENT II: MARGINAL LEXICAL GLOSSES

*Extracted from the working annotations of A. Vane, transcribed from the water-damaged third edition of Jelenić's* Grammatica Vetus Illyrica *(Zara, 1904; rev. 1911). Four entries selected for their structural pertinence to the Cataster. Vane's handwriting deteriorates visibly between entries (ii) and (iii).*

---**(i) *Kamen-pamt* (n., Class III, animate-stone)****Nom. sg.:** *kamen-pamt***Gen. sg.:** *kamen-pamta*
**Abl. of Regret:** *kamen-pamtež*
**Loc. of Vanishing Presence:** *kamen-pamtě*

**Gloss:** Commonly mistranslated as *limestone* or *building stone*. In fact, the noun does not denote the mineral calcium carbonate in its static, geological sense. The root *pamt-* (cf. O.Slav. *pamjatĭ*, memory; cf. also the Illyric substratum *pam-ti*, "the duration for which a thing remains thinkable") specifies that *kamen-pamt* is limestone *as it exists in the decaying impression it leaves upon a perceiving mind*. The stone is not the stone. The stone is the rate at which you will forget the stone. The poché of any wall built from *kamen-pamt* is therefore not a fixed dimension but a function of the observer's mnemonic half-life, and Kovačević's 1911 structural calculations (see the surviving engineering drawings, Archive Folder 7, sheets 14–31) treat the compressive strength of the masonry as directly proportional to the rate of memorial decay in the observer standing beneath it. The faster you forget the wall, the harder the wall bears. The wall is load-bearing *because* you will not remember it.**Structural note:** In the Ablative of Regret (*kamen-pamtež*), the noun encodes the stone *as it was removed from the observer's mind by an act of grief*. This case governs the post-tensioned ferroconcrete tendons in the Sanatorium's primary vaults. The cables are tensioned not to a fixed kilonewton value but to a value derived from the Ablative: the greater the regret, the greater the tensile load the cable must bear, lest the vault, no longer remembered, fall.

---**(ii) *Stĕna-vekt* (n., Class II, inanimate-passage)**

**Nom. sg.:** *stĕna-vekt***Abl. of Regret:** *stĕna-vekta*
**Loc. of Vanishing Presence:** *stĕna-vektě*

**Gloss:** See Fragment I. *Corridor, passage, the space between.* But strictly: *the half-life of one's recollection of having traversed a space between two walls.* The corridor is not the space. The corridor is the memory of the space, and the memory is decaying, and the corridor, in obedience to its own nominal morphology, contracts as the memory contracts. I have measured this. I have measured this three times. The measurement is not stable. The measurement is not—

*[Vane's handwriting becomes cramped, angular. A blot of ink. The next line is in a different pen.]*

The Locative of Vanishing Presence (*stĕna-vektě*) is the case in which the corridor is spoken of as *present only in the act of ceasing to be present*. This case governs the Sanatorium's egress corridors: the doors, the stairwells, the single processional exit to the courtyard. They exist in the Locative. They are there only so long as one is in the process of losing them.

---

**(iii) *Glas-mrtv* (n., Class I, animate-voice)****Nom. sg.:** *glas-mrtv***Gen. sg.:** *glas-mrtva***Abl. of Regret:** *glas-mrtvež***Loc. of Vanishing Presence:** *glas-mrtvě*

**Gloss:** *The voice of the dead*, but this is insufficient. The *Vetus Illyrica* does not permit a noun for a static, preserved voice. *Glas-mrtv* is the voice *as it decays in the memory of the survivor*, and its morphological class (animate) indicates that the language treats the decaying voice as a living organism, a thing that eats and breathes and diminishes. The Ablative of Regret (*glas-mrtvež*) is the form in which the voice is spoken of *after the survivor has, for the first time, failed to recall it accurately*. This case is, in the architectural grammar of the Sanatorium, the case of the load-bearing partition walls. The walls between the patients' cells are conjugated in the Ablative of Regret. They are made of the sound of a voice one can no longer quite hear. They hold up the building. They hold up the building because the voice is gone and the grief is structural and the grief is *load-bearing*.I should not have written this. I should not have looked up this word. Margot's voice was a phonetician's voice, a voice that could isolate the formant frequencies of a vowel and name them like a botanist naming flowers, and I can no longer—I can no longer—

*[The remainder of entry (iii) is illegible. The page is warped, as though exposed to moisture or to prolonged pressure, as though something heavy had been set upon it for a very long time.]*

---

**(iv) *Tiš-grad* (n., Class IV, abstract-masonry)****Nom. sg.:** *tiš-grad*
**Abl. of Regret:** *tiš-gradež*
**Loc. of Vanishing Presence:** *tiš-gradě*

**Gloss:** *The silence that is built.* Not the absence of sound. Not the pause between utterances. *Tiš-grad* is silence understood as a construction material, as a substance with compressive and tensile properties, as a thing that can be quarried, cut, coursed, and set in mortar. Kovačević's apostasy from Wagner and Loos consisted precisely in this: where Wagner sought the *Gesamtkunstwerk*, the total work in which all arts fused into a single architectural utterance, and where Loos sought the elimination of ornament, the stripping of the wall to its mute, rational surface, Kovačević sought the elimination of the wall itself, or rather its replacement with a substance that was not stone and not void but *organized silence*, silence cut to dimension, silence bearing load, silence in which the patients' voices would be absorbed not as sound is absorbed by felt but as a word is absorbed by the grammar that declines it, so that the patient who spoke within the *tiš-grad* did not echo but was *conjugated*, was *parsed*, was entered into the syntax of the building and held there in the Locative of Vanishing Presence, present only in the act of ceasing to be present, a voice in the wall, a voice that was the wall, a voice that held up the ceiling because the ceiling was made of the forgetting of that voice, and the forgetting was structural, and the forgetting was—*[Entry (iv) ends mid-sentence. The following page has been torn out. The stub is clean. The tear is deliberate.]*---

## FRAGMENT III: THE COUNTERFACTUAL CODICIL

**SANATORIUM DEL SILENZIO — MONTE NEBULOSO****Board of Governors, Internal Memorandum**
**Classification: Restricted (Hydrographic Commission Eyes Only)****Date: 11 March 1928**
**Ref: SdS/Phys-Acoust/1928/044**

**RE: Physiological Adaptation of the Vocal Apparatus in Long-Residency Patients; Acoustic Coupling with Parabolic Vault Structures; Recommendations for the Modification of the Morning Liturgy**To the Chairman of the Board, Dr. Ferenčić, and to the attending physicians of Wards III through VII:This memorandum is submitted in compliance with the Board's directive of2 January last, requesting a consolidated report on the respiratory and phonatory anomalies observed among patients resident in the Sanatorium for a period exceeding fourteen months. The findings are, I must state at the outset, without precedent in the otolaryngological literature, and I submit them with the greatest reluctance and with the strong recommendation that this document be sealed in the Commission's archive and not circulated beyond the signatories named below.

The anomaly is as follows. The parabolic vaults of the Sanatorium—designed by the late Ing. Kovačević to a focal ratio of 1:3.7, lined with a proprietary lime-andite composite whose acoustic impedance has been measured at0.004 rayls, a value I am informed is lower than that of any naturally occurring or manufactured substance—do not reflect sound. They do not absorb sound in the conventional sense, as a felt baffle or a perforated panel might absorb it. Rather, and I must ask the Board to credit me with the gravity of a man who has examined thirty-seven larynges by direct laryngoscopy and who does not make such claims lightly, the vaults *decline* sound. The acoustic energy entering the parabolic field is subjected to a transformation analogous to, and I use the term with full awareness of its impropriety, *grammatical inflection*. The fundamental frequency is preserved, but the formant structure—the resonant peaks that give a vowel its identity, that distinguish an /a/ from an /o/, that make a voice recognizably a *human* voice and not a tone—is systematically altered. The patients do not hear echoes. They hear their own utterances returned to them *in a different case*, as though the vault has taken the nominative of their speech and handed back the ablative, and what they hear is not their word but the *regret of their word*, the word as it would sound if it were spoken by someone who had already forgotten why they spoke it.

The physiological consequences are as follows, and I set them down clinically, as the Board requires:

In patients resident for fourteen to twenty months, the intrinsic muscles of the larynx—the thyroarytenoid, the cricothyroid, the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoids—begin to atrophy and reorganize. The vocal folds, which in a healthy adult vibrate at between85 and 255 Hz depending on sex and register, thicken and lose their laminar structure. The mucosal wave, that travelling undulation of the epithelial surface which is essential to normal phonation, is replaced by a *standing wave*, a fixed oscillation that does not propagate along the length of the fold but vibrates in place, in situ, as though the vocal cord has become a structural element, a *tie-beam*, a *lintel*, a horizontal member bearing load. The patients do not lose their voices. They lose the *voluntariness* of their voices. They speak, but the speech is not produced by the intentional contraction of the laryngeal musculature; it is produced by the resonant coupling of the vocal folds to the parabolic field of the vault above, so that the patient becomes, in the strictest mechanical sense, a *component of the building's acoustic structure*, a vibrating element in the Sanatorium's own phonatory apparatus, and the words they produce are not their words but the building's words, the building speaking through them in the *Vetus Illyrica*, in a language they did not know before admission and cannot forget after discharge, if discharge is permitted, which, in the cases I have examined, it is not.

In patients resident beyond twenty-two months, the adaptation extends to the supralaryngeal tract. The pharyngeal constrictors remodel. The soft palate calcifies along its posterior margin, producing a rigidity that eliminates velopharyngeal port closure and forces all phonation into a permanent, open-throated resonance that matches, to within2 Hz, the fundamental mode of the nearest parabolic vault. The patients can no longer close their mouths to produce bilabial stops. They can no longer raise the tongue tip to the alveolar ridge for dental consonants. They can produce only the open vowels, the nasals, the glottal fricatives—the sounds that require no closure, no contact, no *articulation*, only the passive channel through which the vault's resonance passes. They become, in the terminology of the phonetician Dr. Margot Vane, whose preliminary survey of 1968 remains the only external acoustic analysis of the Sanatorium's interior, *pure formants without a source*, resonant cavities shaped by the building to resonate at the building's frequency, and Dr. Vane's notes on this point, found in her effects after the accident of '69, contain a marginal annotation in red ink that reads simply: *They are not speaking. The building is speaking. They are the grammar.*

I recommend, and I do so with the full weight of my office and my twenty-three years of service to this institution, that the Morning Liturgy be suspended. That the parabolic vaults of Wards V through VII be lined, if it is possible, with a material of higher acoustic impedance. That the remaining patients be transferred to the coastal facility at—

*[The memorandum ends here. The final page is missing from the Commission's file. A handwritten note in the margin of page three, in a different hand, reads: "The building does not permit the recommendation. The building declines it. See the Locative." The note is unsigned. The ink is the colour of lime mortar.]*---

## FRAGMENT IV: THE DISINTEGRATING STREAM OF CONSCIOUSNESS

*[Recovered from the field log, 19 September 1973. The handwriting begins in Vane's standard copperplate and deteriorates progressively. The final paragraphs are written in a hand that the Commission's graphologist has described as "consistent with extreme fatigue or with the motor patterns of a person writing in a language they are in the process of forgetting."]*

The diphthong. The wretched, small, *insignificant* diphthong in the Locative of Vanishing Presence of *glas-mrtv*, the voice of the dead, I wrote it with the second element as /e/ when the lexicon, when Jelenić's grammar, when Margot's own red-ink annotation on page 217 specifies /ɛ/, the open-mid, the *open* vowel, the vowel that requires the jaw to drop, the mouth to open, the throat to be *unsealed*, and I wrote the close /e/, the sealed vowel, the vowel that closes the mouth like a door, like a lintel, like the *tiš-grad*, the silence that is built, and I corrected it. I corrected it. I took the graphite stylus and I crossed out the /e/ and I wrote the /ɛ/ and I thought I was being *precise*, I thought I was being a *philologist*, I thought I was honouring the grammar, and the sound I heard when the stylus crossed the paper was not the sound of graphite on paper, it was the sound of a wall being built, a single course of ashlar being laid in a bed of lime mortar, a *thick, slow, calcium sound*, the sound of calcium hydroxide reacting with atmospheric carbon dioxide and crystallizing into calcium carbonate, into stone, into *kamen-pamt*, into the forgetting-stone, and I looked up from the page and the door, the single processional egress, the *stĕna-vekt* that leads to the courtyard and the harbour and the Hydrographic Commission and the city where Margot's laboratory is locked and chalk-dusted, the door was gone. Not closed. Not locked. *Gone*. In its place, a wall of smooth, unhewn limestone, warm to the touch, warm as a living thing, warm as the inside of a mouth, and the surface was not rough but *vocal*, it had the texture of a palate, the ridged, grooved texture of a hard palate behind the upper teeth, and when I pressed my ear to it I heard, not silence, not the *tiš-grad*, but a sound I know, a sound I knew, a sound I used to know, the sound of Margot's voice saying the open-mid /ɛ/, saying it into the spectrograph microphone in the laboratory on the Via delle Mura, saying *eh, eh, eh* in her patient, pedagogical voice, the voice she used for the first-year students, the voice that meant *listen, listen, this is how the vowel is shaped, this is how the jaw drops, this is how the mouth opens*, and I pressed my ear to the wall and the sound was there but it was *curing*, it was *setting*, it was undergoing the slow chemical transition from liquid to solid, from voice to stone, from the living /ɛ/ to the crystalline, the mineral, the *architectural* /ɛ/, and the formant frequencies were shifting, I could hear them shifting, F1 dropping from600 Hz to 480, to 390, to a frequency below the range of human hearing, and the voice was becoming a *load-bearing frequency*, a structural resonance, a vibration in the calcium carbonate lattice, and I would never hear it again as a voice, I would hear it only as a wall, as a *kamen-pamt*, as the rate at which I forget the sound of her saying *eh*, and the forgetting is structural, the forgetting holds up the ceiling, the forgetting is the *tiš-grad*, and I am standing in a room with no door and the walls are made of my forgetting and the ceiling is made of my forgetting and the floor is made of my forgetting and I cannot—

I cannot decline this. I cannot conjugate this. There is no case in the *Vetus Illyrica*, there is no case in any language, for the moment in which the memory of a voice becomes a wall, for the moment in which the sound of a woman saying a vowel is *petrified*, is *coursed*, is *set in mortar*, and I am the surveyor, I am the one who measures, and I cannot measure this, the theodolite will not hold the angle, the graphite stylus will not mark the distance, because the distance is *conjugating*, the distance is declining through the Ablative of Regret, the distance is being *regretted away*, and the room is smaller than it was an hour ago, and the walls are warm, and the walls sound like a palate, and the light is the grey light of stone remembering illumination, and I am going to sit down, I am going to sit on the floor of the Peristyle of Aorist Inflections, which is no longer a peristyle, which is no longer aorist, which is *perfective*, completed, finished, sealed, and I am going to press my palms to the warm stone and I am going to say her name in the active voice, *I say Margot, I say Margot, I say Margot*, and the walls will hold, the walls will hold, the walls will hold, because if I stop speaking in the active voice the room will decline into the passive and the passive is the case in which the room *is had*, in which the room *is possessed by the grammar*, in which I am not the surveyor but the *surveyed*, in which I am the *kamen-pamt*, the forgetting-stone, the rate at which the room remembers me, and the rate is slowing, the rate is slowing, and I can feel the poché closing, I can feel the walls drawing their slow, calcium breath, and I say *Margot*, and the sound is not a sound, the sound is a *course of ashlar*, the sound is a *lintel*, the sound is a *tiš-grad*, and I am building her into the wall, I am building her into the wall, I am building her into the wall, and she is *load-bearing*, and she will hold, and she will hold, and she will hold, and I will never hear the vowel again except as the sound of mortar curing in the dark, and the dark is *conjugated*, and the dark is *declining*, and the dark is—

*[The log entry ends. The remaining pages of the notebook are blank. The graphite stylus was found embedded in the wall of the Peristyle at a depth of4 centimetres, as though it had been pressed into wet plaster and the plaster had subsequently cured.]*

---

## FRAGMENT V: THE FINAL LITHOGRAPHIC REGISTER**AUSTRO-VENETIAN HYDROGRAPHIC COMMISSION**
**Office of the Exclave of Kotor-Grado**
**Paleographic Cataster, Final Entry****Object:** Sanatorio del Silenzio, Monte Nebuloso**Location:**42°27′N, 18°46′E (coordinates approximate; the exclave's cartographic survey has been suspended pending resolution of the Hydrographic Commission's jurisdictional status)
**Architect:** Ing. Dragutin Kovačević (1883–1919), pupil of Otto Wagner, expelled from the Akademie der bildenden Künste, 1909; subsequent association with the Loos atelier terminated by mutual repudiation,1910.
**Construction:** 1911–1916. Limestone (*kamen-pamt*, local quarry), post-tensioned ferroconcrete, lime-ite composite vaulting. Seven wards, one peristyle, one nave, one crypt (unexcavated). Total enclosed volume: indeterminate. See Note 1.**Condition as of survey date,15 August2026:**

The structure stands. The word *stands* is used here in its most literal and most attenuated sense. The Sanatorio del Silenzio occupies the ridge above the harbour in the manner of all large limestone buildings in this region: heavily, silently, with the particular inertia of a thing that has been in place so long that the landscape has accreted around it, so that the distinction between the building and the geology is no longer clear, so that the cypress roots in the eastern courtyard have grown into the stereotomic joints of the foundation courses and the salt wind has effaced the tool-marks on the ashlar to a smoothness that is not the smoothness of wear but the smoothness of *completion*, of a surface that has finished being worked and has begun, very slowly, to forget that it was ever a surface at all.

The Peristyle of Aorist Inflections is accessible via the eastern transept, though the word *accessible* requires qualification. The corridor measures, as of the present survey, 11.2 metres in length. The1911 engineering drawings specify 43 metres. The poché of the lateral walls measures 3.7 metres, a thickness inconsistent with any known structural requirement for a single-storey processional space and more consistent with the walls of a *crypt*, a *vault*, a *chamber designed to bear a load that has not yet been applied*. The hypaethral oculus is intact. The light that enters through it is grey, diffuse, and appears to originate not from the sky but from the stone itself, as though the limestone has absorbed a century of Adriatic sun and is now, in its slow calcium way, *remembering* it.

The Nave of the Perfective is sealed. The Apodyterium of the Southern Wing is sealed. Wards III through VII are sealed. The seals are not locks, not boards, not welded steel plates. The seals are *walls*. Smooth, unhewn, warm limestone, continuous with the surrounding masonry, without joint or seam or evidence of construction, as though they had always been there, as though the doors had never been doors but had always been walls, as though the memory of the doors had decayed to the point at which the stone, obedient to its morphology, had simply *become* wall. The surface of each sealed wall has the texture of a human palate: ridged, grooved, faintly warm. When pressed to the ear, the walls produce a low, continuous resonance at approximately 112 Hz, which corresponds to the fundamental mode of the nearest parabolic vault. No speech sounds are detectable. No speech sounds are detectable. The resonance is continuous and does not vary with time of day, weather, or the presence of observers.

**Note 1:** The total enclosed volume of the Sanatorio cannot be determined by standard surveying methods. The theodolite readings taken from the exterior do not correspond to the interior dimensions. The interior dimensions do not correspond to each other. The Peristyle measures11.2 metres from the east but 34 metres from the west. The Nave, viewed through the sealed arch of the Apodyterium, appears to recede to a vanishing point that is not on the horizon but *below the floor*, as though the perspective has been declined into a case for which Euclidean geometry has no name. The Commission's cartographer has declined to produce a plan. The Commission's cartographer has declined, in all senses of the word, and has not returned to the exclave since October of last year.**Note 2:** In the crypt, which is accessible via a stair in the Nave that was not present during the 1973 survey and whose provenance cannot be established, there is a single chamber, roughly circular, approximately 4 metres in diameter, with a domed ceiling of lime-ite composite. The walls are covered, floor to apex, in a dense, regular script, incised into the stone with a graphite stylus. The script is in the *Vetus Illyrica*. It is a continuous, unbroken text, without paragraphing, without punctuation, without the spacing between words that would permit the identification of individual lexemes. It has been examined by three philologists. All three agree that the text is grammatically coherent. All three agree that it is written entirely in the active voice. All three agree that it appears to be a *survey*, a *measurement*, a *cataloguing* of the dimensions of the chamber itself, and that the dimensions recorded in the text do not match the dimensions of the chamber in which the text is written, and that the discrepancy between the two sets of dimensions is *exactly equal* to the rate of decay of a human memory over a period of fifty-three years. The graphite stylus is embedded in the wall at a depth of4 centimetres. It is warm to the touch.**Note 3:** The Sanatorio is unoccupied. There are no patients. There are no physicians. There is no Board of Governors. The Austro-Venetian Hydrographic Commission, which commissioned the original survey and which has maintained jurisdiction over the exclave since the Congress of Vienna, will be dissolved by ministerial decree at the end of the present fiscal year. The files pertaining to the Sanatorio have been transferred to the Commission's archive in the harbour office. The archive is locked. The key is in the possession of the archivist, who has not been seen since February. The archive, when examined through the window, appears to contain a single room, roughly circular, approximately4 metres in diameter, with a domed ceiling, and the walls are covered in a dense, regular script.

**Note4:** The Sanatorio is unoccupied. The Sanatorio is unoccupied. The Sanatorio is unoccupied. This fact is recorded three times in accordance with the Cataster's protocol for the notation of *tiš-grad*, the silence that is built, which requires that the absence of sound be stated once for each of the three persons of the verb, so that the silence is not merely *observed* but *conjugated*, so that the silence is not a void but a *structure*, so that the silence bears load, so that the silence holds up the roof, so that the silence is the roof, so that the silence is the building, so that the building is the silence, so that the silence is—

**Status:** Standing.**Status:** Standing.**Status:** Standing.

I uncase the transit. The instrument—a Troughton & Simms micro-metric theodolite with an unlacquered brass limb—tarnishes within forty paces of the threshold, coated in the pale, alkaline condensation that sweats continuously from the groin-vaults.

The peristyle does not conform to the Tuscan ideal of Wagner’s early municipal sketches, nor to the absolute ornament-negation of Loos’s *Michaelerplatz* interiors, but constitutes an apostasy between them: cyclopean stereotomy of Istrian limestone faced with post-tensioned, slag-aggregate ferroconcrete, the seams filled not with bitumen but with an unslaked calcitic lime that hums faintly at the lower threshold of audibility.

I place the sight-vane upon the stylobate of the northern colonnade. When I advance along the longitudinal axis, setting the steel chain against the plinth (*I drive the bronze pin; I draw the tape; I record the interval of eight meters and forty centimeters*), the bays exhibit a severe, expansive classical entasis; the hypaethral lantern above admits a sharp, salt-whitened shaft of Adriatic light, through which the dust of pulverized sea-shells falls in undisturbed vertical columns. The spatial register remains nominative, active, legible. 

Yet, as the fatigue of the ascent overtakes me and my notes shift from the active declaration of measure to the recorded state of being measured—*as the chain is dragged across the flags, as the plumb-line is suspended in the damp updraft, as the distance between the third and fourth pier is observed to lessen*—the cyclopean poché of the perimeter walls visibly thickens.

The masonry breathes inward. The intercolumniation, verified thirty minutes prior at 8.40 meters, compresses under the passive grammatical mood to 5.12 meters; the transverse arches drop three decimeters along their springlines; the hypaethral aperture closes like an ocular sphincter, choking the daylight into a thin, violet seam. 

```
STATION OBSERVATION LOG (TRANSIT CHRONOLOGY):
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
11:04 CET | Nominative Act:   "I calculate the span."     | Span: 8.40m (Clear)
11:26 CET | Medial Reflexive: "The span reveals itself."  | Span: 6.88m (Dusk)
11:49 CET | Passive Oblique:  "A measurement is suffered."| Span: 3.10m (Poché closed)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

The walls are not closing through mechanical subsidence. The limestone is not shifting on its karst bedding-planes. Rather, the void between the piers is being retracted because the passive construction lacks an agent to sustain the void’s historical necessity. 

To document this sanatorium in the standard Italian or German of the Commission is to precipitate an immediate structural thrombosis. I must revert to the declensions of the *Vetus Illyrica*—a tongue in which every noun carries an inherent velocity of oblivion, and in which a room exists only so long as the speaker assumes full syntactic liability for its eventual forgetting.

#### Item 402/a:
Sanatorio del Silenzio, situated on the western scarp of Monte Nebuloso, above the Canale di San Girolamo. Construction initiated May 1911 under the direction of Aurel Koloman; abandoned November 1928 following the dissolution of the regional sanitary authority; resurveyed October 1973 by the Department of Epigraphy.

#### Description:
The structure, as it exists in the present year, presents no openings, doors, hypaethral courts, fenestrations, or accessible interior volumes. 

Contrary to the earlier cadastral cartography of 1908—which indicated an open peristyle, a convalescent gallery consisting of four parabolic pavilions, and an extensive system of ventilated subterranean cisterns—the entire site now forms an unbroken, monolithic block of Istrian limestone and post-tensioned ferroconcrete measuring ninety-two meters in length, forty-four meters in breadth, and eighteen meters in height. 

The exterior masonry exhibits an exceptionally fine stereotomy, the ashlar blocks being fitted without visible joints or external mortar lines. No tool marks are visible upon the stone facings, which are everywhere finished to an absolute, unornamented smoothness corresponding to the radical modernistic directives of the early Loosian school.

A core-drill sample extracted from the geometric center of the mass (Core Sample A-1, depth 14.2 meters) by the engineers of the Trieste Port Authority revealed no voids, pipes, or architectural poché. The structural matrix consists of a continuous, highly consolidated aggregate of calcium silicate hydrate, micro-crystalline calc-spar, and iron rebar. 

At a depth of eleven meters, the drill intercepted a dense petrographic anomaly: a pocket of carbonaceous matter containing high concentrations of calcium carbonate, trace amounts of lead graphite, a distorted brass vernier scale calibrated in thirty-thirds of a millimeter, and a fossilized human mandible whose alveolar processes are entirely fused to the surrounding limestone matrix.

The structure is dry. It possesses no acoustic resonance. It requires no maintenance. Its mass is invariant under all conditions of measurement.
